explanation: The decision to extend depends on the result, which makes it another look at the data, so the chance of a false positive goes up, even if nobody looks again until the new end. If more power is needed, the team should plan a new test with a fresh sample size. Reading 0.09 as significant moves the threshold after the result, which is the same mistake. More data in a pre-planned test is good; more data added until the p-value crosses the line is the mistake.
